text:
Jonathan Marchessault returned to Nashville's lineup on Nov. 17 after a two-week absence and scored against Minnesota, his third goal of the season. It's a nice beat for a 35-year-old who won the Conn Smythe with Vegas in 2023 and built a career as an undrafted free agent.

The harder truth is in how his shifts go. At five on five the Predators take only 35% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 14 points worse than without him, and that's not a small-sample fluke on its own: Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with opponents getting more chances against him than against all but 3% of forwards.

He still earns his keep on the power play, where five of his six points have come. His chance quality is down to 0.71 expected goals per 60 from 0.90, and his shooting is at 8.8%. Fifteen games is not enough to write him off, but what we'd watch is whether Nashville keeps giving him even-strength minutes or narrows him into a power-play specialist.
headline: Marchessault is back, and the questions are too
